transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Start: 14:10 PST
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Karen Holt (Midtown Head of ML), Luis Ramirez (VP Eng), Samir Patel (Cloud Architect)

Auto-summary: Quick discovery to understand traffic profiles and security posture for a Dedicated deployment. Customer wants reserved GPUs for predictable throughput, VPC isolation, and a burst strategy for end-of-day batch jobs. They asked about SSO, KMS, audit logs and model fallbacks.

---
00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we got about 45 minutes on the calendar. i'm alex from redwood, and with me is priya from our solutions eng team. can you do quick intros?
00:12 Karen: sure i'm karen holt, lead on ml for midtown bank, been working on conversational assistants and doc ingestion pipelines. we've got some late night batch jobs and also realtime chat for agents.
00:22 Luis: luis ramirez, vp engineering, i'll be owning infra decisions and cost sign-offs.
00:28 Samir: samir patel, cloud architect, i'll be looking at vpc, networking, and how to integrate with our kms.
00:34 Priya: great, quick agenda — sizing and capacity, isolation needs, burst handling, security/compliance, and next steps. sound good?

02:00 Alex: high level question — are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private? what's leaning?
02:06 Karen: leaning dedicated. we like the API for hosted but we need isolation and predictable performance. also need to ensure no cross-tenant data leakage for PCI-adjacent workloads.
02:18 Luis: and cost predictability — we have a predictable baseline qps during daytime hours and then big spikes EOD and monthly reconciliation windows.

05:12 Priya: ok can you give us rough qps and sequence lengths so we can size GPUs? 
05:20 Karen: baseline is about 40 requests/s, avg seq len 256 tokens, peak for spikes maybe 300 requests/s for 10-15 minutes during end-of-day. monthly batch runs hit sustained 150 requests/s for 2 hours.
05:36 Priya: got it; are your workloads streaming generation or single-shot completions?
05:42 Karen: mostly single-shot completions for transcripts and summary, some streaming for agent chat but that's lower volume.

08:05 Priya: for dedicated we typically recommend reserving a base pool sized for baseline throughput and then configuring burst capacity — either through burst pools or by allowing controlled overflow to hosted. any preference on overflow?
08:20 Samir: overflow to hosted is tricky due to data residency. we prefer isolated burst capacity that stays within our VPC if possible.
08:30 Alex: yep we support Dedicated with private subnet attachments so bursts can be contained — there are two options: 1) reserved burst nodes in your dedicated pool that stay idle until needed, or 2) autoscale ephemeral nodes with your cloud provider but still within your VPC (depends on on-prem vs cloud setup).
08:52 Luis: what's the typical spin-up time for ephemeral nodes? we can't have minutes of cold start for peak windows.
09:00 Priya: warm nodes are fastest — for our orchestration we can keep a small hot pool so spin-up is sub-30s, cold nodes could be a couple minutes. if you want millisecond latency for spikes, reserved burst nodes are the way to go. there's a cost tradeoff.

12:15 Karen: what about KV cache and prefix caching for repeated conversations? can that help with cost?
12:24 Priya: yes, persistent KV/prefix caching reduces per-token compute and can route recurring sessions to cached state. for dedicated we can persist cache to local NVMe on the node or to a managed cache. caveat: if you want strict disk encryption and KMS integration we can enable that. sometimes transcription will show 'k v cache' in docs, sorry transcription.

14:40 Alex: on isolation — you mentioned PCI-adjacent. do you need an on-prem air-gapped option or is VPC with customer-managed KMS sufficient?
14:50 Karen: VPC + CMK is probably sufficient, but procurement will want SOC2/ISO papers and audit logs. they may push for an on-prem option for specific workloads later.
15:08 Alex: we can provide SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts, plus audit log retention options. we also support HSM/KMS integrations and bring-your-own-key for encrypting model inputs/outputs at rest.

17:30 Luis: how do you handle model rollouts and fallbacks if a particular GPU type is down? we can't risk downtime during peak windows.
17:40 Priya: we have smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants. for Dedicated you can pin model versions and also set automatic fallback policies to either a slightly smaller model or to a hosted fallback in a different region. fallback to hosted again runs into data residency concerns though.

20:05 Samir: network egress — we need to ensure no egress outside our region for certain data classes.
20:12 Alex: we support region pinning and can deploy Dedicated pools in their desired region. egress controls and VPC egress rules can be configured; we can also provide a private control plane.

23:00 Priya: operationally, what SLOs are you targeting for tail latency?
23:06 Karen: 95th perc < 400ms for chat, 99th < 1s is stretch but desirable. batch jobs can be slower.
23:20 Priya: with dedicated GPUs and batching configurations we can get average token latency in single shot completions well under that for a 256 token seq on optimized kernels; 95th depends on batch sizing and concurrency — we'll run a benchmark.

26:10 Luis: cost — how do you charge for Dedicated? is it flat for reserved capacity plus per-token?
26:18 Alex: Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) with an hourly cost for the reserved nodes. for bursts there are options: reserved burst nodes (included in commit) or pay-as-you-go burst at a higher rate. we also provide tooling (Redwood Optimize) to recommend quantization and batching to reduce unit costs.

29:00 Karen: ok procurement will want a sample contract and an escalation path for incidents.
29:08 Alex: we have enterprise SLAs and a premium support add-on; i'll send the contract outline and escalation matrix.

31:45 Samir: security questionnaire — we'll send you the RFP security sheet, can you respond?
31:52 Alex: yes we'll pass that to our security team; priya will own the technical responses. send it to security@redwood.example and cc me.

34:20 Priya: one more technical detail — model quantization and mixed precision: are you comfortable with 4-bit quantized models for cost savings or do you require FP16/FP32 for quality?
34:30 Karen: we need to validate on our eval sets. quality is paramount for customer-facing agent responses, but for internal summarization quantization is fine.

36:50 Alex: recap and next steps — we'll size a base pool for 40 rps at 256 tokens, recommended reserved burst to cover 300 rps short spikes, propose warm pool to keep spin-up under 30s, send pricing and SOC2 docs, and schedule a benchmark run w/ Priya.
36:58 Karen: yep that sounds right.

39:10 Luis: timeline — we're looking to have a pilot in 4-6 weeks and a production commit in 2-3 months depending on procurement.
39:20 Alex: workable, we'll prioritize the benchmarking and security pack this week.

41:00 Karen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security questionnaire and sample traffic.

---
Action items mentioned in call:
- Priya to run capacity estimation and recommend node types (NVidia H100 vs A100 tradeoffs)
- Alex to send pricing, contract outline, SLAs, and SOC2 pack
- Customer to send traffic profile and security questionnaire

References shared: Redwood dedicated overview deck (link provided in chat), SOC2 summary doc, example benchmark template.

End of transcript.
